**Step 1 — Scene:** A small spinach-based salad with a short corn-on-the-cob round and a little broccoli.

**Step 2 — Vessel:** A roughly 27 cm square dinner plate. Using the requested circular approximation: 3.14 × 13.5² ≈ **572 cm²**. Food on the neighboring plate is excluded.

**Steps 3–7 — Items, coverage, volume, weight, and energy:**

| Visible item | Plate area | Gross volume calculation | Bulk density | Estimated weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Spinach leaves and stems | 35% | 200 cm² × 2 cm = 400 ml | 0.15 | 60 g | 23 | 14 kcal |
| Corn round, edible portion* | 5% | 29 cm² × 2 cm = 58 ml | 0.6 | 35 g | 96 | 34 kcal |
| Broccoli pieces | 2% | 11 cm² × 2 cm = 22 ml | 0.6 | 13 g | 35 | 5 kcal |
| Small onion pieces | 1% | 6 cm² × 0.5 cm = 3 ml | 0.7 | 2 g | 40 | 1 kcal |
| Small pepper/vegetable slivers | 1% | 6 cm² × 0.7 cm = 4 ml | 0.6 | 3 g | 30 | 1 kcal |
| Light oily dressing, suggested by the sheen | Overlaps leaves | Approximately 4 ml | 1.0 | 4 g | 880 | 35 kcal |

Food footprints total approximately **44%** of the plate; dressing overlaps rather than adding coverage.

*Corn weight estimates the edible kernels, not the central cob; this is the least certain volume-to-weight conversion.*

**Step 8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **117 g edible food and 90 kcal** is plausible for this modest, loosely piled salad. Dressing quantity is the main source of energy uncertainty.
